invariants.text: mechanism.json covers both engines: auction (pure-bid vs quality-weighted GSP vs first-price with bid shading, including the GSP-not-truthful demonstration and the RGSP/pricing-knob coda) and distribution (AOL 2002 economics, TAC series, network share, default-payment economics, Mehta findings).
Every worked example's arithmetic re-computes exactly from its stored steps.
Empirical numbers (deal terms, TAC, shares) carry full calibration objects; invented example numbers are marked as illustrative, never calibrated.

The capture-attribution analysis states its verdict on auction-vs-distribution with explicit evidence weights, and the twin engines are reconciled into one account (no contradiction between the two analysts' outputs).
invariants.instructions: Read mechanism.json and mechanism-notes.md. The merged analysis must take a documented stance with evidence, and nothing in the auction section may contradict the distribution section on the same fact.

invariants.text: simulator-params.json is buildable: every scenario ties to a claim or break it demonstrates, every variable has range and default, expected outputs are stated per scenario, and every mechanism claim the chapters will make has a covering scenario (including the first-price/bid-shading panel).
invariants.instructions: Cross-reference simulator-params.json scenarios against mechanism.json claims. A mechanism claim with no covering scenario, or a scenario with undefined variables or missing expected output, violates this invariant.
